title: Cumulative use of proton pump inhibitors and risk of dementia: the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study
authors: Northuis CA, Bell EJ, Lutsey PL, George KM, Gottesman RF, Mosley TH, et al.
followUp: median 5.5 years after visit 5 (2011 to 2013), through 2017
population: Dementia-free ARIC participants at visit 5, mean age 75.4 years, 22% Black, 58% female; PPI use from visual medication inventory since 1987 to 1989
funder: The Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study is conducted as a collaborative study supported by NIH National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute contracts; neurocognitive data are collected by NIH grants (NHLBI, NINDS, NIA, NIDCD); this work was also supported by NHLBI training grant T32 HL007779 and K24 HL159246.
authorConflicts: E.J. Bell is employed by Optum and has received funding from Novartis, Incyte, AstraZeneca, EMD Serono, Sandoz, Celgene and Pfizer; other authors report NIH funding or no disclosures.
result: 585 incident dementia cases. Current PPI use at visit 5: HR 1.1 (95% CI 0.9 to 1.3). Cumulative use above 4.4 years before visit 5: HR 1.3 (1.0 to 1.8), described as 33% higher risk; shorter durations were not significantly associated.
